subject: SummitWay service: throughput spike, elevated errors — exec action & customer update
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: [ALERT] SummitWay - sustained throughput spike + error rate increase

Team —

Telemetry picked up an anomalous pattern for SummitWay between 07:30-08:05 PT: sustained client qps increased ~3x above baseline for the payments route, associated with a jump in 5xx error rate to ~7% (baseline ~0.3%). P95 latency for generation tokens has crept from ~320ms to ~1.2s for affected shards.

Quick facts (from initial snapshot):
- Customer: SummitWay (prod region: us-west-2)
- Model variant: redwood-13b-opt-v3 (serving pool: dedicated-4)
- Peak sustained QPS: 3600 (baseline ~1200)
- Error profile: 5xx spike mostly 503/504 and occasional tokenize/fallback errors
- Latency: P50 ~420ms, P95 ~1.2s, tail P99 hitting ~2.8s

I attached the telemetry snapshot and raw logs we pulled from the nodes (summitway_service_logs_0429.zip). Initial hypothesis: sudden input distribution shift causing cache churn + kernel contention on two GPUs in pool-4.

Recommend immediate steps:
1) Stand up a brief exec bridge (30–45m) — propose 08:30 PT.
2) Apply targeted routing to move SummitWay traffic to alternate pool (dedicated-5) and enable conservative batching limits (max batch size 8).
3) Warm KV cache for high-frequency prefixes where we see repeated prompts.
4) Prep a short customer-facing note with what we know + next update ETA.

Marissa — can you lead comms with SummitWay? Laura / Monica — can you confirm whether pool capacity for dedicated-5 is healthy and ready to receive traffic?

Karthik
(on-call — Inference Reliability)

Attachments: telemetry_snapshot_0429.json, summitway_service_logs_0429.zip

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Anya Voss <anya.voss@summitway.com>

Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 08:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [ALERT] SummitWay - sustained throughput spike + error rate increase

Thanks Karthik — pulling this together now.

Anya / SummitWay ops team — we see a sudden sustained increase in request volume to your production integration that has caused elevated error rates and higher tail latency. We’ve stood up an internal incident bridge and are executing mitigations now. Primary customer-facing points:
- What happened: brief surge in request patterns that is leading to cache eviction and higher GPU kernel contention, increasing 5xx responses and tail latency.
- What we’ve done so far: engineering is routing traffic to a warm pool and applying tighter batching caps; we’ve identified hot prefixes and are warming caches.
- Next update: 30 minutes (approx 08:45 PT).

Immediate ask for SummitWay: if you can temporarily reduce non-critical background traffic (bulk analytics calls) that will help drop the QPS pressure while we stabilize.

I’ll send a short one-page status note for your leadership and will keep this channel for live updates.

Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Anya Voss <anya.voss@summitway.com>
Cc: SummitWay Support <ops@summitway.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SummitWay service: throughput spike, elevated errors — exec action & customer update

Summary from the bridge and immediate mitigation steps (live as of 08:55 PT):

Root cause hypothesis (brief):
- Sudden spike in long prompt reuse from an internal SummitWay batch job — high prefix churn causing KV cache thrash on pool-4 GPUs.
- Combined with a kernel scheduling pressure on 2 of 6 GPUs in the pool due to an OS-level bug that surfaces under high concurrency (we have a trace).

Actions taken / in progress:
- Traffic has been shifted incrementally to dedicated-5 (healthy capacity) — initial cutover at 08:42 PT, full routing by 08:52 PT.
- Conservative batching enforced (max batch size=8) and per-client rate cap applied to the summitway key.
- KV cache warmers activated for the identified prefixes; we’ve pre-populated hot entries.
- For immediate customer protection we enabled automatic retriable response handling (no opaque drops; most failures are retriable 5xx at the gateway). We are not seeing duplicate charge patterns in the logs; payment handlers are idempotent — still validating with SummitWay logs on their side.

What we expect next: error rate down to <0.5% within 15 minutes of full cutover; tail P95 to return under 500ms within ~20–30 minutes as caches and queues stabilize.

Attachments: mitigation_playbook_0429.md (internal runbook), telemetry_snapshot_0429.json

Laura Bennett
Director, Inference Reliability | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Anya Voss <anya.voss@summitway.com>, SummitWay Support <ops@summitway.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: SummitWay incident - afternoon readout and next steps

Anya / SummitWay leadership —

Final readout from today’s incident and customer commitments: thanks for your patience.

Timeline (condensed):
- 07:30 PT: surge detected; 5xx increase observed.
- 08:12 PT: internal alert and bridge stood up.
- 08:42–08:52 PT: traffic migrated to healthy pool and batching caps applied.
- 09:10 PT: error rate returned to baseline (<0.4%); latency P95 returned to ~360ms.

Confirmed outcomes:
- No confirmed permanent transaction loss — failures were retriable at the gateway layer; payment handlers remained idempotent. We will continue a joint log reconciliation for absolute confirmation.
- Root cause: high-volume long-prefix batch job from SummitWay causing KV cache churn + a GPU kernel scheduling bug exposed under that load.

Commitments:
1) Redwood will run a follow-up joint-forensics session with SummitWay infra on Mon 05/03 at 09:00 PT to review logs and confirm no client-side duplicates. We will share a combined timeline and artifacts.
2) We will proactively add a per-client early-warning rule for abnormal prefix churn and a temporary safeguard to preempt this exact mode of failure.
3) As a goodwill gesture for the business disruption, Redwood will propose a one-time credit against April usage; I’ve looped in our account lead to draft terms.

Action items (owners):
- Laura: deep trace analysis + OS-level kernel scheduling follow-up (deliverable: root-cause doc, 05/01).
- Karthik: incident postmortem and playbook updates (deliverable: 04/30).
- Marissa: prepare formal customer incident report & credit proposal (deliverable: 04/30).
- SummitWay: confirm any duplicate transactions from your side and share webhooks/logs (owner: Anya).

If there are any concerns or additional asks, reply directly on this thread. We’ll publish the joint artifacts to the HubSpot deal and to the shared Drive link.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: customer_status_note_0429.pdf
